title: Trends Across the AI Frontier — George Cameron, ArtificialAnalysis.ai
talk_summary: A benchmarking talk showing that model choice involves multiple frontiers (intelligence, cost, speed, verbosity), with reasoning models using ~10x more output tokens and latency, and cost-per-intelligence falling >100x in two years. The core actionable message is to measure cost/latency per completed task, not per-token price, and to match model tier to task.

takeaways.technique: Measure cost per task, not per-token price
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a fixed eval suite through each model and report total dollars and total output tokens consumed, exposing that verbose reasoning models cost far more than their per-token price suggests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're paying for the cost per token but then you're also paying for how verbose the models are
takeaways.numbers: O3 cost $2,000 to run their intelligence index; GPT-4.1 ~30x cheaper than O1; 4.1 nano >500x cheaper than O3; reasoning models used 7M vs 72M vs 130M output tokens

takeaways.technique: Tier models by task: cheap/fast for volume, reasoning only where needed
takeaways.what_they_do: They separate non-reasoning (cheaper, faster, less intelligent) from reasoning models and argue you should not always use the most intelligent model; match tier to latency/cost budget.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You shouldn't always use the leading most intelligent model
takeaways.numbers: GPT-4.1 median 4.7s vs O4-mini-high >40s; ~10x latency gap

takeaways.technique: Account for latency multiplication across sequential agent steps
takeaways.what_they_do: They model agent latency as per-call latency times number of sequential calls, showing order-of-magnitude per-call differences compound.
takeaways.numbers: 30 calls at 10s = 300s (5 min) vs 30 calls at 1s = 30s

takeaways.what_they_do: They run a consistent composite benchmark across all models so comparisons are apples-to-apples, and urge builders to measure trade-offs themselves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'd encourage everybody to measure them
takeaways.numbers: Composite index of seven evaluations across 150+ models

takeaways.technique: Benchmark review recall per model, not just pass/fail gate
takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish intelligence from verbosity and cost, implying the 'best' model for a task must be measured on that task's outcome.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's more than one frontier in AI ... There's trade-offs to accessing this intelligence

takeaways.technique: Design for falling cost, revisit rejected architectures
takeaways.what_they_do: They show cost of a fixed intelligence level halving within months of a new frontier, and advise building as if cost weren't a barrier because it may become feasible.
takeaways.numbers: Cost of GPT-4-level intelligence fell >100x since mid-2023; new-band cost halved within months
